title: Native sign-in and browser pairing: separate approval, saved identity and access
goal: Navigate the finite native/browser sign-in controls without confusing HTTP approval, selected saved credentials, secure-storage persistence, entitlement or current operation authority.
prerequisites: Internal source-only draft; A5 clean-host acceptance remains unfinished. Current installed-version/platform support, current service and entitlement require separate evidence.

Native handoff requires validated HTTPS service origin (loopback HTTP development exception only), exact connect origin/challenge/intent and stored device fingerprint. No credentials, passwords, live challenges, codes or tokens belong in this record.

Browser approval requires current signed-in user/organization and inspected pairing policy: valid nonplaceholder device fingerprint/label and active-session limit. Policy asks revoking an existing pairing at session cap, but no revocation control is documented here.
permissions: Browser identity pairing, native candidate verification/durable selected credential and commercial entitlement are distinct; none supplies provider-wide approval/execution permission.

Native candidate verifies before committing credential plus selection in one vault value, then activates transport. Explicit selection prevents cross-identity fallback; selected missing/invalid/expired credential requires sign-in. Only installations lacking selection metadata retain legacy API-key-first compatibility.

Rejected identity locks transport/clears displayed identity but retains vault data; unavailable failures can expose saved retry. Current context/generation and cancellation guards discard stale results.

Source secureStorage delegates packaged calls to native commands; outside Tauri memory-only. This article does not invoke or qualify OS storage consent, Keychain, clean-host behavior or restart durability.

recovery: Invalid/expired/consumed challenge: return to Agent for a new explicit sign-in. Do not bypass device binding or infer challenge-only success;426requires existing signed-installer guidance/new attempt.
Browser account mismatch: explicit Use another account affects browser only, then review again; cannot replace an already approved challenge. Browser Cancel is navigation, not revocation/abort.
HTTP authorized/deep-link failure: Open Axiom Agent is manual fallback, then independently verify native selected identity/save. Do not treat HTTP/deep-link attempt as durable success.

Saved retry is only offered for unavailable verification; preserves selected identity, does not create pairing/write selection. Rejected/invalid/expired saved identity requires explicit sign-in rather than fallback.
Review legitimate OS prompt without sharing keys in support; no embedded Keychain button. Storage/save failure remains unconfirmed and requires displayed guidance, not unsupported persistence claims.
Current verified identity may still lack entitlement. Check access again or follow separate legitimate access/billing process; navigation/focus is not access grant.
Logout/account-change cleanup failure preserves signed_out selection but can leave older values. Retry legitimate cleanup when storage available; no external workflow rollback claim.
